sections.label: Overview
sections.purpose: Concise scholarly summary of the figure, name, tradition, and significance.
sections.body:
**Padmasambhava** (*padmasambhava*) — Lotus-Born, Vajrayana, Tibet · 'Lotus-born' (padma 'lotus' + sambhava 'born, arisen'), 'Guru Rinpoche', the tantric master revered as the founder-figure of Tibetan Buddhism. — belongs to the Buddhist tradition, where it is catalogued under the domain "Lotus-Born, Vajrayana, Tibet". The name means "'Lotus-born' (padma 'lotus' + sambhava 'born, arisen'), 'Guru Rinpoche', the tantric master revered as the founder-figure of Tibetan Buddhism.".

**Padmasambhava** is lotus-born, vajrayana, tibet. The name means "'Lotus-born' (padma 'lotus' + sambhava 'born, arisen'), 'Guru Rinpoche', the tantric master revered as the founder-figure of Tibetan Buddhism." and belongs to the buddhist tradition.

PuniCodex restores the name as **Padmasambhava** and serves its temple at [its temple](https://punicodex.com/padmasambhava/). The restoration needs no distinctive letters or diacritics its ASCII form would lose, which places the name in Tier 2. The plain ASCII form *padmasambhava* survives as a modern convenience imposed by the early domain-name system; the restoration, not the fallback, is the form the project defends as philologically complete.

sections.label: The Name
sections.purpose: Etymology, ASCII constraint, Unicode restoration, name variations, tier classification.
sections.body:
The name is attested in Devanagari as **पद्मसम्भव**. Etymologically it means "'Lotus-born' (padma 'lotus' + sambhava 'born, arisen'), 'Guru Rinpoche', the tantric master revered as the founder-figure of Tibetan Buddhism.".

The ASCII form *padmasambhava* survives only because the early domain-name system could not carry diacritics; it is a technological compromise, not an ancient spelling. The Unicode restoration **Padmasambhava** recovers the full diacritic detail of the scholarly transliteration directly in the address bar. The restoration needs no distinctive letters or diacritics its ASCII form would lose, which places the name in Tier 2.

sections.body:
The reconstructed pronunciation of the name is **/padmasambhava/** — Restored scholarly form.

Phoneme by phoneme:

- **padmasambhava** — The canonical restored form Padmasambhava.

For the modern speaker, the closest approximation is: Say "padmasambhava" with the stress and length implied by the scholarly restoration "Padmasambhava".

The ASCII form "padmasambhava" is a DNS compromise; the restoration "Padmasambhava" preserves the name's scholarly dignity.

The pronunciation given above reconstructs the sound world in which Padmasambhava was invoked. Modern speakers should not expect exact identity with ancient phonology; the reconstruction is a scholarly compass, not a performance prescription. The restoration Padmasambhava keeps the prosodic information visible even when the name is typed in plain ASCII.

sections.label: Original Script & Provenance
sections.purpose: Original writing system, transliteration steps, uncertainty markers, font/display notes.
sections.body:
The name is preserved in Devanagari as **पद्मसम्भव**.[^1]

The scholarly transliteration is *Padmasambhava*.

The rendering proceeds step by step:

- Sanskrit Padmasambhava is written in Devanagari as पद्मसम्भव
- IAST transliteration maps each Devanagari vowel and consonant to a Latin equivalent
- Macrons mark long vowels (ā, ī, ū); dots beneath consonants mark retroflex articulation (ṭ, ḍ, ṇ, ṣ)

sections.label: Mythology
sections.purpose: Core myths, primary narratives, and textual evidence.
sections.body:
The stories of Padmasambhava place lotus-born, vajrayana, tibet at the center of a living mythological world.

### Origins (Myth)

Padmasambhava appears in buddhist tradition as lotus-born, vajrayana, tibet. The name's meaning, "'Lotus-born' (padma 'lotus' + sambhava 'born, arisen'), 'Guru Rinpoche', the tantric master revered as the founder-figure of Tibetan Buddhism.", shapes the narratives told about this figure.

### Worship and Memory (Cult)

Devotees and later tradition-keepers preserved Padmasambhava in ritual, text, and iconography, ensuring the name survived into the modern scholarly record.

The myths of Padmasambhava survive in fragments, summaries, and later retellings. Each version reflects the interests of its tellers — poets, priests, philosophers, and scholars. The PuniCodex entry does not privilege a single version; it gathers the attestations so that readers can compare them. The restoration Padmasambhava gives the figure a stable name around which these variants orbit.

Within the Buddhist tradition, closely related names in the corpus include [[akshobhya|Akṣobhya]], [[amitabha|Amitābha]], [[amoghasiddhi|Amoghasiddhi]], [[arhat|Arhat]], [[asanga|Asanga]], and [[avalokiteshvara|Avalokiteśvara]].

Cross-cultural identifications are rarely one-to-one. Padmasambhava may be likened to figures in neighboring traditions without being identical to them. The PuniCodex crosslink index records these resonances as relationships, not equations. The restored form Padmasambhava makes such comparisons possible across language boundaries.

sections.body:

The PuniCodex temple participates in that afterlife by ensuring that the restored name Padmasambhava remains findable and citable.

sections.label: Archaeology & Material Evidence
sections.purpose: Sites, inscriptions, artifacts, and physical attestations.
sections.body:
No monument, inscription, or artifact in the current PuniCodex corpus is yet assigned to Padmasambhava with certainty. That absence should be read honestly: for a Buddhist name of this type the material record is expected to be thin, and the primary evidence remains the textual testimony gathered in the Scholarly Sources section.

Were such evidence to surface, it would take recognizable forms: votive or dedicatory inscriptions naming पद्मसम्भव, sanctuary or cult remains tied to lotus-born and iconography matching its traditional attributes (name and domain). Each candidate would be weighed against the reconstructed form of the name before entering the scholarly record.

sections.label: Pāli Canon
sections.body:
The Pāli Canon preserves the earliest stratum of Buddhist scripture in Middle Indic. While Padmasambhava often belongs to later Mahāyāna elaboration, the canonical values of mindfulness, compassion, and liberation underpin the figure's significance.

The restoration Padmasambhava follows IAST convention used in Buddhist studies.

sections.label: Mahāyāna Sūtras
sections.body:
Mahāyāna sūtras expand the cult of Padmasambhava across Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan transmissions. Texts such as the Lotus Sūtra, Avataṃsaka, and Pure Land sūtras place the figure in expansive cosmologies of buddhahood and bodhisattva activity.

The IAST form Padmasambhava marks the Sanskrit reconstruction behind those transmissions.

sections.label: Meditation & Reflection
sections.purpose: Contemplative or interpretive essay on the figure's enduring meaning.
sections.body:
To contemplate Padmasambhava is to hold the idea of lotus-Born, Vajrayana, Tibet in the mind and to ask what of it endures. The name means "'Lotus-born' (padma 'lotus' + sambhava 'born, arisen'), 'Guru Rinpoche', the tantric master revered as the founder-figure of Tibetan Buddhism." — and a name that carries its meaning so openly invites meditation rather than mere recollection. The tradition remembers the name as lotus-Born, Vajrayana, Tibet · 'Lotus-born' (padma 'lotus' + sambhava 'born, arisen'), 'Guru Rinpoche', the tantric master revered as the founder-figure of Tibetan Buddhism..

Sit with the restored form — Padmasambhava — and the diacritics themselves become the practice: each mark is a small act of attention, a refusal to let the plain ASCII form *padmasambhava* stand in for the whole. What the tradition preserved in this name, the restoration asks the reader to preserve in turn.
